# Health It

This folder catalogs digital health applications and pharmaceutical products used in the management and treatment of Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD) within the Danish healthcare system. It features the Constant – Care app, a digital tool for remote patient monitoring and biomarker testing, alongside several modern biologic and small-molecule drugs—including etrasimod, filgotinib, mirikizumab, ozanimod, risankizumab, and upadacitinib. The drug pages specifically document their recent integration into the Danish National Patient Register (Landspatientregisteret) via new administrative treatment codes, enabling their inclusion in national clinical quality reporting.

## Pages

- [[constant-care|Constant – Care]] — A digital patient application used at Nordsjællands Hospital for remote monitoring and point-of-care calprotectin testing in IBD patients.
- [[etrasimod]] — An S1P receptor modulator for IBD that received a new SKS treatment code in the national patient register in April 2025.
- [[filgotinib]] — A small-molecule IBD treatment assigned a new registry code in 2024 to enable tracking of fecal calprotectin measurements in national quality reports.
- [[mirikizumab]] — A modern biologic IBD therapy integrated into the national patient registry in 2024 to support clinical quality indicator tracking.
- [[ozanimod]] — A pharmaceutical IBD drug that received a new administrative treatment code in 2024 to close previous gaps in national registry data.
- [[risankizumab]] — An advanced IBD biologic assigned a new registry code in 2024 to facilitate accurate national tracking of treatment outcomes.
- [[upadacitinib]] — A JAK inhibitor for IBD that was added to the national patient registry in 2024 to improve the monitoring of medical therapy quality metrics.
